events.title: Finding Stillness: Letting go of Anxiety through Meditation
events.description: Meditation offers a quiet refuge from the noise of anxious thoughts, helping you return to the present moment with greater ease. By stilling the mind and body, you create space between yourself and the worries that often feel overwhelming. This practice can soften the intensity of anxiety, improve emotional wellbeing and build a sense of inner calm. Even a few minutes a day can become a powerful tool for grounding, clarity, and resilience in the face of life's uncertainties. There will be a chance to practice this technique. Join Arlene Samsel for this workshop. Brief bio of Arlene Samsel: Arlene Samsel is uniquely qualified and experienced in meditation, public speaking, and the performing arts. She has been an elementary school teacher and has also performed publicly as a musician for many years. In addition, Arlene was director of a camp where she taught children how to meditate. She has been meditating for 25 years and has given many meditation workshops and retreats which have enabled her to speak firsthand about the crucial role of meditation in enhancing the daily lives of busy people. Arlene and her husband have raised a family of 3 children and reside in New Brighton, Minnesota.
events.blurb: Join an online meditation session where you practice stilling the mind and body to ease anxious thoughts and return to the present.

We meet virtually on the last Thursday of each month to discuss one or two contemporary short stories (no more than 40 pages total). Participate from anywhere—jump in late or leave early if needed! Registration is required to receive the Zoom meeting link. 2026 Reading List: June 25th - "The Shroud" in Heart Lamp by Banu Mushtaq; July 23rd - "Mall of America" by Suzanne Wang in The Best American Short Stories 2024; August 27th - "A Sunny Place for Shady People" in A Sunny Place for Shady People by Mariana Enriquez; September 24th - "Dominion" by Lauren Acampora in The Best American Short Stories 2025. * Also available in New England Review, Vol 45, No. 2 - available through Gale Academic Onefile with your library card. October 29th - "A Fur Coat" and "Boots" in Night Side of the River by Jeanette Winterson
events.blurb: Join an online short-story book club on Thursday evening to discuss Jeanette Winterson's "A Fur Coat" and "Boots" with fellow readers.

events.title: Storytime with Julia Moss
events.description: Join us for a special storytime with author Julia Moss as she shares her debut picture book, Wanderers: A Walk Through Time and Transportation. Since the beginning we've been on the roam. Searching for food, adventure, and home… Set off on a journey through history and see how many ways humans have dreamed up to travel. First, there was walking, camel-riding, and canoes. Then, the invention of the wheel brought bikes, trains, and automobiles. Next, we took to the air with airplanes and rockets, and now there are new breakthroughs in sustainable travel every day. And what's at the heart of each advancement? Human curiosity and inventiveness.
events.blurb: Hear author Julia Moss share her debut picture book, Wanderers: A Walk Through Time and Transportation, at a Sunday morning storytime.

events.title: Hilo: The Holiday Special with Judd Winick
events.description: We are incredibly excited to welcome New York Times bestselling author-illustrator Judd Winick to the store to celebrate the Hilo Holiday Special! Judd will talk about the latest adventure in his bestselling Hilo series, take questions from the audience, and then sign books. RSVP Now » This event is free, but you must purchase a copy of Hilo: The Holiday Special from Linden Tree to enter the signing line. Books can be purchased with an event ticket, in person at Linden Tree, or on our website. The decorations are up! The gifts are wrapped! And Hilo and the gang are enjoying some holiday togetherness. Sure, it would be better if the skating pond wasn't blocked off. And if someone wasn't stealing trees from the tree lot. And if a giant, super grumpy snowman wasn't going around destroying things. But what's a holiday without holiday surprises?! Can Hilo and friends figure out what the snowman wants before D.J.'s big family party?! Packed with family and food, love and laughter (lots of laughter!) — gather around and enjoy all the gifts of the season with Hilo!
events.blurb: Hear Judd Winick talk about the latest Hilo adventure, ask him questions, and get your books signed.

events.title: Storytime with Seina Wedlick
events.description: Join us as we welcome local author Seina Wedlick back to the store to celebrate her new picture book, Noor and the Storyteller, about a girl who fills the starry, moonlit sky with magical tales. Every night, Noor listens for the sound of the gong and the storyteller's drum. Gong, Gong, Gong! Tap! Tap! Tap! With each beat, fantastic tales swirl and sway and unfold around her. One night, she waits and waits, but no drumbeat comes her way. Can Noor tap the drum and keep the storyteller's magic alive? Find out in this modern fairy tale about a young Nigerian girl who taps stories on her drum and carries tradition in her heart.
events.blurb: Meet local author Seina Wedlick at Linden Tree Books and hear her read from her new picture book, Noor and the Storyteller.

events.title: Fall Art Workshop with Isabella Kung
events.description: Calling all young artists ages 10-13! Join us this fall for a series of hands-on art workshops led by talented, published illustrators. This month's teacher/illustrator is Isabella Kung, author-illustrator of Nunu and the Sea, No Snowball!, and more. Each workshop lasts 90 minutes and costs $75. Materials (paper, pens, etc) will be provided and, at the end of each workshop, students will receive a signed copy of one of the featured illustrator's books. Space for each workshop is limited. Buy tickets now »
events.blurb: Make art alongside illustrator Isabella Kung, author-illustrator of Nunu and the Sea and No Snowball!, in a hands-on workshop for ages 10-13.

events.title: Book Launch with Nathan Hale
events.description: We are incredibly excited to welcome New York Times bestselling author-illustrator Nathan Hale to the store to celebrate the launch of Nathan Hale's Hazardous Tales: The Web of War! Nathan will talk about the latest adventure in his bestselling Nathan Hale's Hazardous Tales series, take questions from the audience, and sign books. RSVP Now » This event is free, but you must purchase a copy of The Web of War from Linden Tree to enter the signing line. Books can be purchased with an event ticket, in person at Linden Tree, or on our website. In the summer of 1944, the Allied forces carried out the largest seaborne invasion in military history. American, British, and Canadian soldiers took to the skies and the sand, bombarding the beaches of Normandy, France in the famous operation known as D-Day. This pivotal battle turned the tides against the Nazis, but how did the French find themselves overtaken by enemy forces to begin with? How did Hitler and his Nazi ideology sweep through Germany so quickly? And how did American military service members and civilians, from generals, to war correspondents, to heroic Black soldiers, work together to defeat the Nazi government and bring an end to Hitler's reign of terror? In The Web of War, history is in your hands! Pick your path and unravel the thrilling, shocking, gruesome, and true stories of the Second World War in this all-new hazardous tale.
events.blurb: Meet New York Times bestselling author-illustrator Nathan Hale at the launch of Nathan Hale's Hazardous Tales: The Web of War.

events.title: I Am Human: Storytime + Creative Writing Workshop
events.description: Calling All Humans! Join author-illustrator Laura G. Lee for a special I Am Human book launch, storytime, and creative workshop. Laura will begin with a reading of I Am Human and a playful conversation inspired by the book: What does it mean to be human? How are we different from AI—and how do we know? After the reading, participants are invited to join a hands-on writing and drawing workshop, responding to creative prompts through words and pictures, enjoying snacks, and sharing ideas. All ages are welcome. The workshop is especially well suited to older elementary kids, teens, and adults, while younger children are welcome to enjoy the story time portion with their families. Workshop RSVPs are encouraged so we can prepare enough materials.
events.blurb: Hear Laura G. Lee read I Am Human, then join a playful conversation about what it means to be human.

events.title: Book Launch with Lily Berlin Dodd — In conversation with Misa Sugiura
events.description: We're excited to welcome New York Times bestselling author Lily Berlin Dodd back to the store to celebrate the launch of the second book in her Aerimander Chronicles series, The First Flame! Lily will be in conversation with author Misa Sugiura. With Eva locked away in Byrdhaven and Rubi missing, all Dusty can do is avoid capture and (attempt to) sleep through his nightmares in the wake of Cal's death. When fate leads Dusty back to the Lockwood Inn, he overhears the next stage of Eoin Parnassus' sinister plans for aerimanders, and knows he must do everything in his power to stop it. Dodging strict nuns, wanted posters, seasickness, altitude sickness, a clockwork army, and a perilously evil clown on the way, Myrnie, Eva, and Dusty are willing to fight to the ends of the Earth--or at least the edges of their map--to stop Eoin Parnassus, Director of Kingdom Secrets. But Rubi is hiding a shocking truth and Parnassus may pose an even bigger threat than they could ever have imagined. Who can be trusted when secrets lurk around every corner of the Kingdom?
events.blurb: Hear Lily Berlin Dodd talk with author Misa Sugiura about The First Flame, the second book in her Aerimander Chronicles series.

events.title: Storytime with Kanya Sesser and Nisha Lamsam Ligon
events.description: Join us as we welcome Kanya Sesser and Nisha Lamsam Ligon to celebrate their empowering new picture book, No Legs, No Limits, inspired by Kanya's childhood and her journey to finding her voice, independence, and freedom on a skateboard. Kanya Sesser was born without legs, but that doesn't mean she has limits! Sometimes I still fall. But I never give up. I make things work for me. Because I'm strong. Because I'm free. Because I have NO limits. Kanya Sesser has spent her life sharing the message that no matter what life deals you, you can do anything. In this picture book based on her childhood, she tells the story of how she first learned to stand up for herself, both on a skateboard and in life. When people grab her wheelchair, to push her to class or onto the bus after school, she's too shocked and too sad to say no. The people around her don't understand that she moves herself. But when she rides a skateboard for the first time, she experiences a new sense of freedom and joy, and she finally finds her voice.
events.blurb: Meet authors Kanya Sesser and Nisha Lamsam Ligon at Linden Tree Books and hear their picture book No Legs, No Limits, inspired by Kanya's childhood and her skateboarding journey.

events.title: Middle Grade Book Club: The Wish Ring Cipher
events.description: It's the next meeting of our middle grade book club for ages 9+! Led by bookseller extraordinaire Lorilee, we hope to introduce interested readers to amazing new books and the opportunity to talk about them in a fun, relaxed group setting. This month's book is The Wish Ring Cipher by Alexandra Ott, a fast-paced adventure novel filled with puzzle solving, a hint of magic, and new school fears. Please email lorilee@lindentreebooks.com to RSVP. Emma Avery has always loved solving puzzles and codes, and now that she's processing a recent autism diagnosis and facing down seventh grade at a new school, they're even more important to her. Then Emma meets Nate Lin. He's popular and funny and... loves codes, too. He introduces Emma to the Codebreakers, a group of his friends dedicated to cracking codes that have been discovered in the ruins of a nearby ghost town, which are believed to lead to magical objects. But they're not the only ones on the hunt, and when their sinister rivals close in on an object that grants unlimited wishes, the Codebreakers must race to beat them to it before they use it for dark magic.
events.attendanceNote: For readers ages 9 and older. Email the bookstore to RSVP using its events calendar.
events.blurb: Talk about The Wish Ring Cipher with fellow readers ages 9 and up at a middle grade book club led by bookseller Lorilee.

events.title: Facing Reality Without Losing Your Peace of Mind

events.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Academic Excellence
events.description: This workshop helps middle and high school students engage with Artificial Intelligence as a meaningful partner in their academic pursuit, rather than a shortcut. Through guided, hands-on learning, participants develop key skills in prompt engineering, research synthesis, and AI-supported organization using tools like Gemini, Notebook LM, and Google Workspace. Grounded in critical thinking and mindful use, the program emphasizes right use, source verification, and proper citation practices. Students learn to evaluate information, build well-supported arguments, and organize ideas into clear, structured academic work. By the end of the session, participants will be confident in using AI responsibly to enhance their learning towards their academic curriculum in an increasingly AI-driven world.

events.title: ELL Beginning English: The Basics
events.description: Do you want to build your English-language skills and your confidence? Participants will have the opportunity to learn & develop their speaking, listening, reading and writing skills. Suggested for beginner English language learners. The ELL Beginning English program meets weekly at the library in the library's Community Room with a trained facilitator. Free. No registration required. events.description: ¿Estás cansado de no poder hacer cosas tecnológicas por ti mismo? ¿Cansado de esperar a que los miembros de tu familia te ayuden o hagan las cosas por ti? ¡Ahora puedes aprender a hacer todo eso por ti mismo! Tenemos personas pacientes y serviciales disponibles para ayudarte a aprender cualquier tema relacionado con la tecnología. Nunca es tarde para aprender a usar la tecnología. ¡Solo llámanos! La biblioteca te brindará apoyo para: Abrir una cuenta de correo electrónico; Conectarse a un hotspot/Wifi; Usar Chromebooks/computadoras; Usar Zoom; Encontrar e inscribirse en clases de la biblioteca; Obtener una tarjeta de la biblioteca; Reservar materiales; Usar aplicaciones de la biblioteca; Teléfono móvil; Busca en internet. Este es un programa presencial organizado en la Sucursal de la Biblioteca Latinoamericana. El personal de la biblioteca o un voluntario estarán allí para guiarte en todo, pero serás tú quien controle la computadora. Si no puede asistir a su cita, llame y cancele. Se dará prioridad a los clientes que no falten a sus citas. Gratis. Se requiere registro. Para registrarse, llame al (408) 294-1237.
events.blurb: Practice doing tech tasks yourself with personalized, Spanish-language help at the Biblioteca Latinoamericana, so you can stop waiting on family for help.

events.title: Spooktacular Haunted House
events.description: Get ready for some spooktacular fun! Families are invited to make their way through our family-friendly Haunted House in the Community Room, featuring several spooky stations, including a creepy cemetery, spider web corner, and more Halloween surprises. After your haunted adventure, stop by the Children's Area for a free book and candy giveaway while supplies last. This event is designed for children and their families, so expect more fun than fright. Halloween costumes are welcome and encouraged; Haunted House: Community Room; Book & Candy Giveaway: Children's Area, while supplies last. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Walk through a family-friendly haunted house in the Community Room, with stations like a creepy cemetery and a spider web corner.

events.title: ESL Conversation Club: Beginning (Tiếng Việt)
events.description: Xây dựng kỹ năng giao tiếp với những người học trình độ mới bắt đầu khác trong một môi trường chào đón và tôn trọng. Khóa học này sẽ sử dụng Confidence and Connections và Mango Languages. Sử dụng tài nguyên điện tử này miễn phí với thẻ thư viện. Mỗi buổi học được hướng dẫn bởi nhân viên thư viện có thể nói được tiếng Việt. Miễn phí. Phải đăng ký và làm bài kiểm tra xếp lớp. Build conversation skills with other beginner-level adult learners in a welcoming and respectful environment. This course will use Confidence and Connections and Mango Languages. Use this e-resource for free with a library card. Each session is led by library staff who can speak Vietnamese. Free. Registration & placement testing required.
events.blurb: Practice beginner English conversation skills with fellow learners in Vietnamese at Seven Trees Library.

events.title: 1-on-1 Tech Help / Trợ Giúp Kỹ Năng Máy Tính Bằng Tiếng Việt
events.description: This event is offered in Vietnamese. Are you or your loved ones struggling with using a smartphone, downloading apps, or making video calls to see the family? Come join our Free One-on-One Tech Mentor Support sessions. We can help you with: Basic help for smartphones, tablets, and computers; Downloading and using everyday apps; Making video calls (Zoom, FaceTime, Google Meet) to stay connected; Exploring AI tools and answering your AI questions/concerns; Navigating our library website and wonderful digital resources. Note: Our support is focused on basic technology questions. Drop-ins are accepted. How to make an appointment: Priority will be given to patrons with appointments, so please book yours today! Call us at: (408) 808-3060. Email Rebecca Quan at: Rebecca.quan@sjlibrary.org. Có cô chú hay ông bà, cha mẹ mình đang gặp chút khó khăn khi dùng điện thoại thông minh, tải ứng dụng, hay muốn gọi video để gặp con cháu mà chưa biết cách không ạ? Quý vị hãy ghi danh cho người thân để họ tham gia chương trình Hỗ trợ Công nghệ 1-kèm-1 miễn phí. Chúng tôi sẽ hướng dẫn tận tình các kỹ năng sau: Sử dụng điện thoại, máy tính bảng và máy tính cơ bản; Cách tải và sử dụng các ứng dụng hữu ích; Cách gọi video (Zoom, Google Meet...) để kết nối với gia đình; Giải đáp các thắc mắc về AI mới; Cách tra cứu trang web của Thư Viện San Jose và sử dụng các tài nguyên số bổ ích. Lưu ý: Chương trình tập trung hỗ trợ các câu hỏi và thao tác công nghệ cơ bản. Chào đón quý vị tới gặp nhân viên thư viện nếu có câu hỏi đơn giản. Cách thức ghi danh: Xin ghi danh đặt hẹn trước (thư viện sẽ ưu tiên cho người có lịch hẹn): Gọi điện thoại: (408) 808-3060. Hoặc gửi email cho cô Rebecca Quan: rebecca.quan@sjlibrary.org Hosted by Evergreen Branch. #dsb Digital Skills
events.blurb: Get one-on-one help in Vietnamese with smartphone basics, app downloads, and video calls to family at Evergreen Library.

events.title: English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club
events.description: Berryessa Branch Library presents an in-person adult English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club. Are you looking for a place to practice your English conversation skills in a fun, welcoming and safe environment? Our English Language Learners (ELL) Conversation Club offers a respectful environment for adult learners of English to practice their English speaking & conversation skills used in everyday settings. All levels of English-speaking skills are welcome! Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Practice your English conversation skills with other learners in a welcoming club setting.

events.title: ESL Workforce Development Workshop - Day 5: Present Yourself with Confidence
events.description: Join us for a five-session workshop designed for ESL learners who want to strengthen their workplace communication skills. In addition, participants will develop basic digital skills by learning how to use Google Workspace tools (Docs, Slides, and Drive) and Canva to create professional documents and presentations that can support job searches, interviews, and career advancement. Participants should be able to communicate in basic English (speaking, reading, and writing). Workshop Topic: Present Yourself with Confidence. This is a free program. Registration is required. Talleres de Desarrollo Laboral para Estudiantes Hispanos de ESL Acompáñenos a este taller de cinco sesiones diseñado para estudiantes de inglés (ESL) que desean fortalecer sus habilidades de comunicación en el entorno laboral. Además, los participantes desarrollarán habilidades digitales básicas al aprender a utilizar las herramientas de Google Workspace (Docs, Slides y Drive) y Canva para crear documentos y presentaciones profesionales que les apoyen en la búsqueda de empleo, las entrevistas y el desarrollo de su carrera profesional. Los participantes deben tener la capacidad de comunicarse en inglés a un nivel básico (hablar, leer y escribir). Tema del taller: Preséntese con Confianza. Este programa es gratuito. Es necesario registrarse.
events.blurb: Practice presenting yourself with confidence in a workshop session for ESL learners building workplace communication skills.

events.title: Reading Buddies
events.description: Reading Buddies provides students in grades TK-3 with an opportunity to improve their reading skills by working one-on-one with a trained volunteer or staff member. Reading Buddies creates a positive reading experience for beginning and developing readers and helps children build confidence as readers. Our volunteers will listen to children read and provide support in phonics, sight words, and comprehension. Students can bring their favorite book or choose from the available selection at the Rose Garden Branch Library. Free. Pre-registration not required. However, reading sessions are available on a first-come, first-served basis and the duration of reading sessions may be limited depending on the number of volunteers and/or participating students.

events.blurb: Pair up with a trained volunteer to read one-on-one and build reading confidence.

events.title: Hazlo tú mismo (DIY) para adultos | Adult DIY
events.description: Únase a nosotros en la Biblioteca Latinoamericana para nuestro programa de hacerlo tú mismo. Realizaremos proyectos divertidos durante todo el año. Nuestros proyectos se enumeran por mes a continuación. Se proporcionarán todos los materiales. ¡No es necesario que traiga nada excepto usted mismo y tal vez un amigo o dos! ¡Por favor asegúrese de registrarlos también! 28/08/26 - Decora velas con servilletas; 25/09/26 - Impresión Solar; 30/10/26 - Decora artículos de fiesta con confeti. Gratis. Se requiere registro. Llama al (408) 294-1237 para registrarte. Por favor, entre a la biblioteca por la puerta del lado de la entrada/estacionamiento. Our projects are listed by the month below. All supplies will be provided. No need to bring anything except yourself and maybe a friend or two. Please be sure to register them as well! 08/28/26 - Decorative Candles with Napkins; 09/25/26 - Sun Printing; 10/30/26 - Confetti Party Ware. Free. Registration required. Call (408) 294-1237. events.title: Cricut Open Lab
events.description: The Cricut Open Lab is a 45-minute learning session on select Fridays with machines available to use. First-time users can learn what the Cricut machine is and how it works. You can also watch these tutorial videos ahead of time to get a better idea of how to use the Cricut machine and Design Space. Those who already have experience using Cricut are welcome to register to use a machine independently to cut out their designs. We will have Cricut machines (Explore/Air and Maker), limited supplies, and several designs available for participants. Individuals or groups up to 3 people can register for the program. Registration required. This program is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Vineland Branch Library.

events.title: Everyone Can Code: Rock, Paper, Scissors Using Swift Playgrounds
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Create your own rock, paper, scissors game using Swift Playground! Everyone Can Code is a beginner's course on using iPads to code and modify technology, such as online games. Students will be learning the basics of coding and implementing them through the modification of rock, paper, scissors. Everything needed for this course will be provided, but you are more than welcome to bring your own personal iPad with the free Swift Playgrounds app downloaded, especially if you want to save your work. Free. Registration is recommended. This series is taught in English only. Registration closes at 12 PM the day before class. However, if seats are still available, students in grades 3-6 can walk in on Saturday if they arrive before 3 PM to sign in. Maximum class size is 25. Although the class is scheduled from 3-4:30 PM, students who finish their projects early are welcome to leave early. Todos pueden programar: Piedra, papel o tijera con Swift Playgrounds ¡Crea tu propio juego de piedra, papel o tijera usando Swift Playgrounds! Sábado 31 de octubre de 2026 de 3 a 4:30 horas 'Todos pueden programar' es un curso para principiantes que enseña a utilizar iPads para programar y modificar tecnología, como los juegos en línea. Los estudiantes aprenderán los conceptos básicos de la programación y los pondrán en práctica modificando el juego de piedra, papel o tijera. Todo lo necesario para este curso será proporcionado, pero puedes traer tu propio iPad personal con la aplicación gratuita Swift Playgrounds descargada, especialmente si deseas guardar tu trabajo. Gratis. Se recomienda registrarse con anticipación. Esta serie será enseñada únicamente en inglés. La inscripción cierra a las 12 p.m. el día antes de la clase. Si quedan espacios disponibles, los alumnos de grado 3 a 6 pueden venir el sábado e inscribirse antes de las 15:00 p.m. La clase tiene un cupo máximo de 25 alumnos. Aunque la clase está programada de 3-4:30 p.m., los alumnos que terminan sus proyectos antes podrán retirarse si lo desean. Everyone Can Code: Trò Chơi Kéo-Búa-Bao với Swift Playgrounds Thứ Bảy, ngày 31 tháng 10 năm 2026 từ 3-4:30 giờ chiều Hãy tự tạo trò chơi Kéo-Búa-Bao cho riêng quý vị bằng Swift Playgrounds! "Everyone Can Code" là khóa học dành cho người mới bắt đầu, hướng dẫn cách sử dụng iPad để lập trình và sửa đổi kỹ thuật công nghệ, chẳng hạn như trò chơi trực tuyến. Học viên sẽ học những kiến thức lập trình cơ bản và áp dụng chúng thông qua việc sửa đổi của trò chơi Kéo-Búa-Bao. Mọi thứ cần thiết cho khóa học này sẽ được cung cấp, nhưng bạn hoàn toàn có thể mang theo iPad cá nhân của mình với ứng dụng Swift Playgrounds miễn phí đã tải xuống, đặc biệt khi bạn muốn lưu tác phẩm của mình. Miễn phí. Xin vui lòng ghi danh trước. Lớp học được chỉ dạy hoàn toàn bằng tiếng anh. Thời hạn ghi danh kết thúc vào 12 giờ trưa ngày trước khi lớp học bắt đầu. Tuy nhiên, nếu vẫn còn chỗ trống, học sinh lớp 3-6 có thể đến trực tiếp vào thứ Bảy nếu đến trước 3 giờ chiều để điểm danh. Lớp học tối đa là 25 học sinh. Mặc dù lớp học được lên lịch từ 3 đến 4 giờ 30 chiều, nhưng học sinh nào hoàn thành bài tập sớm có thể về sớm. Yêu cầu các phương tiện cho ADA

Participants will not be able to finish their skulls in one session and should plan to return for the second session to decorate skulls. Session 1: Sunday, November 1, 11:00 AM - 12:30 PM*; Session 2: Tuesday, November 3, 3:30 PM - 5:30 PM. *This program session will take place before the library opens to the public; participants will enter our community room through the doors adjacent to the parking lot. **Sugar skulls not claimed after the program will be discarded. ¡Haz & decora tu propia Calaverita de Azúcar! ¡Ven a celebrar el Día de los Muertos creando una calaverita de azúcar muy especial! events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For November 1st: Topic: Epicurus's Advice: Make Friends and Be Frank with Them "Every friendship is desirable for itself, but it has its origin in personal advantage." Vatican Sayings 23. "We do not need the help of our friends so much as the confidence that our friends will help us." Vatican Sayings 34. "The man continually seeking help is no friend, nor is the one who never links help with friendship. For the one barters kindness for favors, while the other cuts off hope for the future." Vatican Sayings 39. "Of all the things that wisdom provides for the happiness of the whole man, by far the most important is the acquisition of friendship." Principal Doctrine 27. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Chs. 6 (pp. 54-65) and 7 (pp. 66-79). Some Questions to Discuss: What are the two main qualities that make a relationship a friendship, according to Emily Austin's analysis of Epicurus's views on friendship? [Austin, 56-7]; Austin says that "a shared sense of what truly matters" [64] is a core condition for friendship. What is the meaning of this condition? Do our current ideas about friendship coincide with those of Epicurus? What do we value in friendship? What is "frank speech" for you? Why can we be uncomfortable with telling a friend the truth? What is the reason for feeling this way? Can we be frank even with ourselves? A friend vs. Psychologist: where does your preference lie and why?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

events.title: Tai Chi with Nelson Ng
events.description: Join us for Tai Chi sessions with Nelson Ng! In this weekly class, participants will learn the basic principles and the philosophy behind Tai Chi, gaining flexibility and a better sense of balance through slow, gentle movement. Nelson started learning Chen's Tai Chi in 1989 from Master Gene Chen, who was a disciple of Grandmaster Feng Zhi Qiang. Nelson has been teaching since 2014. This class is free and open to beginners as well as those who have previous Tai Chi experience. People of all ages are welcome. You must sign in upon arrival.

Availability of Reading Buddies is on a first-come, first-served basis.

events.title: Tech Mentor / Computer & iPad Assistance
events.description: Tech mentoring and computer 1-on-1 assistance. A volunteer tech mentor / computer coach will be available to help customers increase their computer skills. events.description: Join us to read The Cyberiad by Stanislaw Lem. You can register for the club and get a copy of the book at the adult reference desk. events.title: Peter Fletcher Classical Guitar Concert
events.description: Please join us for a performance by classical guitarist Peter Fletcher, with a program titled "Music of Four Centuries." With a rich history of performances spanning prestigious venues across the United States, Fletcher's captivating music resonates with audiences worldwide. He has been invited to perform at esteemed cultural venues across the US, including Carnegie Hall! Peter will perform music from the new CD, as well as the Bach Chaconne, Usher Waltz by Russian composer Nikita Koshkin, a very special arrangement of the famous Shaker hymn Simple Gifts, and music by Giuliani, Ponce and Tansman. events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents the Spies Among Us
events.description: This is a rare look into the inner workings of a data-driven surveillance state run by one of the most feared secret police forces the world has ever known – East Germany's Stasi. A personal investigation into family secrets by Peter Keup, a Stasi victim-turned-historian, takes a turn when he contacts the men who ran the system. These are the first dialogues between Stasi officers and a victim ever recorded. Through these encounters a terrifying mosaic is built of the lengths people go to maintain power in a dictatorship, as well as the indomitable human spirit that seeks truth and self-determination. Jamie Coughlin Silverman and Gabriel Silverman are award-winning journalists-turned-documentary filmmakers. Their first feature documentary, TransMilitary, won the Audience Award for Best Documentary at SXSW and received critical acclaim. TransMilitary was represented by Cinetic Media and distributed by Gravitas Ventures. It premiered on Logo TV and Amazon Prime. The film screened at more than 100 film festivals worldwide, and the Silvermans were named to the 2018 Top 10 Filmmakers to Watch list by The Independent. The Silvermans are Gotham (IFP) Documentary Lab Fellows, CNN/Film Independent Episodic Lab Fellows. Their work has been supported by the International Documentary Association, Catapult Film Fund, Jonathan Logan Family Foundation, and Frameline Completion Fund. They are the first recipients of funding from the GLAAD Media Institute. Their production company, SideXSide Studios, is a global documentary firm that specializes in consequential and high-visibility non-fiction storytelling. Prior to SideXSide Studios, the Silvermans worked in leading newsrooms. Gabe was a video journalist at The Washington Post where his work was recognized with more than a dozen awards, including an Edward R. Murrow Award for his investigative work, a White House News Photographers Award for Best Documentary, and two Emmy nominations. Jamie was the supervising producer for USA Today Sports, where she led editorial and branded video content strategy. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers.
events.blurb: Watch this documentary tracing a Stasi victim's personal investigation into East Germany's surveillance machine.

events.title: Adult Nonfiction Book Discussion: Nothing to Envy: Ordinary Lives in North Korea
events.description: In November, the Adult Nonfiction Book Group will discuss Nothing to Envy: Ordinary Lives in North Korea by Barbara Demick (2009). The book is based on Demick's interviews over a seven-year period with six North Koreans who escaped the country and the regime. The vast majority of North Koreans know little more of the world beyond their borders than the rest of the world knows about their daily lives under the Kim Jong-il regime. Without easy access to healthcare, experiencing frequent food shortages, life for the average working family in North Korea under Kim Jong-Il's rule is and was grim by Western standards. As of the publication date of this book, ordinary citizens have few if any civil rights and almost no recourse to protest injustice, as complaints and almost any sign of dissatisfaction with the regime could lead to imprisonment. The Adult Nonfiction Book Group meets on the second Sunday of each month at 11 am in Room 201B. All meetings are sponsored by The Friends of the Cupertino Library. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. events.title: Pageturners: What We Can Know by Ian McEwan
events.description: Pageturners read widely, from nonfiction like Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World by Malcolm Harris to fiction like James by Percival Everett to biography like The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI by Fei-Fei Li and graphic novels like The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting Andrey Kurkov (Diary of an Invasion) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. What will we read next? It's anyone's guess. Members suggest books, and then vote on them. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. Our reading list for 2026 follows: My Friends by Fredrik Backman - January; The Wager: A Tale of a Shipwreck, Mutiny and Murder by David Grann - February; South of the Border, West of the Sun by Haruki Murakami - March; Trespassers at the Golden Gate: A True Account of Love, Murder, and Madness in Gilded-Age San Francisco by Gary Krist - April; The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui - May; The Wedding People by Alison Espach - June; Unlikely Animals: A Novel by Annie Hartnett - July; Say Nothing: A True Story of Murder and Memory in Northern Ireland by Patrick Radden Keefe - August; The Frozen River by Ariel Lawhon - September; We'll Prescribe You a Cat by Syou Ishida - October; What We Can Know by Ian McEwan - November; The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay by Michael Chabon - December. You don't have to register, but you will receive a reminder email if you do.
events.blurb: Discuss Ian McEwan's What We Can Know with fellow readers at the Pageturners book group.

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA; October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation; November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County; January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph. D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/
events.blurb: Join the Graphic Novel Book Club at Mitchell Park Library to discuss the group's latest pick, Thursday evenings.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For November 15th: Topic: An Epicurean in Public Life: Justice and Injustice "Justice's greatest reward is peace of mind." Fragment 80. "Justice was never an entity in itself. It is a kind of agreement not to harm or be harmed, made when men associate with each other at any time and in communities of any size whatsoever." Principal Doctrine 33. "Injustice is not an evil in itself. Its evil lies in the anxious fear that you will not elude those who have authority to punish such misdeeds." Principal Doctrine 34. "It is impossible to leave the pleasant life without also living sensibly, nobly, and justly, and conversely it is impossible to live sensibly, nobly, and justly without living pleasantly. A person who does not have a pleasant life is not living sensibly, nobly, and justly, and conversely the person who does not have these virtues cannot live pleasantly." Principal Doctrine 5. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Ch. 8 (pp. 80-91). Some Questions to Discuss: Based on the ideas expressed in the Principal Doctrines, what is Epicurus's view on the source of justice in society? What is the connection that Epicurus draws between injustice and corrosive desires according to Austin's analysis of his views on injustice? Is it easy to be just? Is it hard to be unjust?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

events.title: Master Gardeners: Planning and Planting a Little Fruit Orchard
events.description: Please join us for an informative workshop presented by UC Master Gardeners of Santa Clara County. So you want to plant fruit trees? Excellent! What kind? Are you looking for plums, apricots, peaches, apples or something less common? There are hundreds of varieties of each. How do you choose? How big should the tree be? (There is actually a correct answer!) What are chill hours and how many are good? Semi-dwarf? True dwarf? Multi-graft? How do I plant a new tree? Local nurseries will begin stocking bare root fruit trees in December. Come learn what decisions affect the success of your orchard. Don Bollinger leads the orchard team at the Master Gardener demonstration garden at Martial Cottle Park in South San Jose. He leads year-round hands-on learning and demonstrations of fruit tree management including winter pruning, water, fertilizer, pest management, soil health and fruit variety selection. No need to register, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before.

events.title: Don't Get Scammed This Holiday Season
events.description: Online holiday shopping is convenient, but scammers are counting on you to be busy, rushed, and hunting for a good deal. As more of us turn to online shopping and charitable giving this time of year, fraudsters are getting better at looking legitimate. How can you tell if that website is a real store? Is that unbelievable social media deal actually a bargain, or a trap? And when you donate to a cause, how do you know your gift is going where you intended? Join us for a practical presentation that will help you shop and give with confidence. You'll learn how to: Verify that an online store is legitimate before you enter your credit card number; Read and understand product reviews, including how to spot fake or paid reviews; Recognize counterfeit and nonexistent products advertised on social media; Identify charity scams and make sure your donations reach the people and organizations you want to help. You'll leave with simple tips and a few trusted resources to help you stay safe shopping for the holidays and beyond. Keep on hand all season long. Whether you're a seasoned online shopper or just getting started, this program will help you protect your money, your personal information, and your holiday spirit. Bring your questions and your own stories. Your experience might help a neighbor avoid a scam too! Registration is recommended but NOT required. Register in order to receive a reminder email the day before the event.
events.blurb: Learn how to spot holiday shopping scams and protect yourself online at Rinconada Library on Wednesday morning.

events.title: Author Event with Dr. Carol Peyser
events.description: Please join us to hear Dr. Carol Peyser discuss her book, A Hidden Fate (She Writes Press, October 27, 2026), a literary novel interweaving multiple themes: the emotional consequences of genetic foreknowledge, the weight of family secrets and deceptions, overcoming childhood trauma, and the unexpected conflicts of vision and conviction that can emerge in love relationships. The novel has received a starred Kirkus review, and a Book Life reviewer described it as "great for fans of Lisa Genova's Inside the O'Briens and Abraham Verghese's The Covenant of Water." Early in her career, she directed the Huntington's Disease Clinic at Johns Hopkins Hospital right when predictive testing became available to people at risk for the terrible disease. Dr. Peyser saw first-hand how genetic knowledge — and even the possibility of obtaining it — alters a person's relationship to their future and to their family. Interacting with people deciding what they wanted, or might not want, to know about their future seared these issues into her heart. Later, as a geriatric psychiatrist on the Stanford faculty and in private practice in Menlo Park, she saw these questions multiply. Descendants of those with Alzheimer's disease, major depression, and other heritable illnesses grappled with fears about genetic risk — and with the weight of what to keep private, and what to disclose — to whom, and when. These questions of genetic knowledge, secrecy, and their consequences are at the heart of the book. How does wondering what might be coded in our DNA impact us? How does knowing what lies in our genes change us? How are families impacted by the new possibilities genomic testing raises?
events.blurb: Hear author Dr. Carol Peyser speak at an evening author event at Rinconada Library.

events.title: 5, 4, 3, 2, 1: Drawing with Time and Rhythm
events.description: In this one-hour figure-drawing workshop, participants will draw together with pencils for 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 minute—and sometimes even 30 seconds. We will begin with longer drawing times and slowly move to shorter, faster ones. Participants can try different pencil pressure, movement, and speed as the timing changes. Participants may volunteer to pose for the group. As we draw, we will watch different poses and body movements and follow the changing rhythm together. The timing will be repeated about three times. Participants will make several drawings on 11 × 14-inch paper and one larger drawing on 18 × 24-inch paper, arranging several figures on one sheet. The workshop is open to adults of all levels. No drawing experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi. Materials: All materials will be provided, including 4B pencils, five sheets of 11 × 14-inch paper, and one sheet of 18 × 24-inch paper for each participant. Duration: 60 minutes
events.blurb: Draw with pencils in timed rounds of 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 minute, in a one-hour figure-drawing workshop.

events.title: Korean Calligraphy Workshop: Writing Your Name in Hangul with Flow and Rhythm
events.description: In this 90-minute workshop, participants will use calligraphy brushes, ink, and hanji paper to write their names in Hangul. Because Hangul is based on sound, names from many different languages can be written in Hangul according to how they are pronounced. Participants will see how their names look in Hangul and experience the rhythm of Korean writing through brush movement and repetition. Participants can get help writing their names in Hangul along the way. We will begin with simple brush exercises on hanji paper. Participants will practice moving the whole arm, changing the pressure and speed of the brush, and making different kinds of lines. They will then write their names several times, following the movement and rhythm of each brushstroke. At the end of the workshop, participants will write their names on a hanji fan. No previous calligraphy or Korean language experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi. Materials: All materials will be provided, including calligraphy brushes, ink, hanji paper, and one hanji fan for each participant. Duration: 90 minutes
events.blurb: Write your name in Hangul using calligraphy brushes, ink, and hanji paper in a 90-minute workshop.

events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents the Panama Deception
events.description: A riveting Academy Award-winning critique of the government's history of militarization, made all the more timely by the current war on terrorism. 1993 Academy Award, Best Documentary Feature. Read the Acceptance Speech by Barbara Trent. The Panama Deception documents the untold story of the December 1989 U.S. invasion of Panama; the events which led to it; the excessive force used; the enormity of the death and destruction; and the devastating aftermath. The Panama Deception uncovers the real reasons for this internationally condemned attack, presenting a view of the invasion which widely differs from that portrayed by the U.S. media and exposes how the U.S. government and the mainstream media suppressed information about this foreign policy disaster. The Panama Deception includes never before seen footage of the invasion and its aftermath, as well as interviews with both invasion proponents like Gen. Maxwell Thurman, Panamanian President Endara and Pentagon spokesperson Pete Williams, and opponents like U.S. Representative Charles Rangel (D-NY.), Panamanian human rights workers Olga Mejia and Isabel Corro and former Panamanian diplomat Humberto Brown. Network news clips and media critics contribute to a staggering analysis of media control and self-censorship relevant to any news coverage today, particularly during times of war. Among the film's excellent reviews are: "meticulously researched" (Hal Hinson, Washington Post); "outstanding" (Betsy Sherman, Boston Globe); "tough.... Provocative.... Moving.... Beautifully edited" (Vincent Canby, New York Times); and "lays out simply and forcefully the case against the 'official' version" (Peter Rainer, Los Angeles Times). The Empowerment Project (EP) worked on this production for two years. EP first came to prominence in 1988 with the release of the equally acclaimed Coverup: Behind the Iran Contra Affair. EP is a non-profit media resource center committed to democratizing the media. Each year, hundreds of independent filmmakers use EP's edit facilities and other services. Since its August 1992 release, The Panama Deception has played in 80 cities, including an eight-week run in Seattle and a five-week holdover in New York City. The film appeared in video stores in August 1993. It was cablecast on Cinemax in the United States during October of that same year. Many local affiliates of PBS have broadcast the film but national PBS, however, has refused to broadcast the film despite the Congressional mandate explicitly requiring that both sides of controversial issues be included in PBS's overall programming. Internationally, the film has been broadcast in Australia, Canada, Poland, Hong Kong, France, Spain, Portugal, the U.K., Iran, Israel, Finland, Switzerland, Mexico, Argentina, Japan, Norway, the People's Republic of China, S. Korea, Italy, Turkey, Russia, S. Africa, the Netherlands, the Philippines, Algeria, Malaysia, and Czechoslovakia. A ban on the film originally imposed by the Panamanian government was lifted in March 1993, following strong internal and international pressure. Funding for The Panama Deception has been provided, in part, by: Channel Four in London, Rhino Home Video, the I. Roderick MacArthur Foundation, the Rex Foundation, the Peace Development Fund, the National Council of Churches, the Car Eth Foundation, the Vietnam Veterans of America Foundation, the Funding Exchange/Paul Robeson Fund for Film and Video, The Charles Lawrence Keith and Clara Miller Foundation, Essential Information, the Vanguard Public Foundation, Lucille Banta, Michelle Connor, filmmaker Michael Moore and hundreds of individual donors. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers.
events.blurb: Watch the Academy Award-winning documentary on Panama and discuss its themes of militarization.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For December 6th: Topic: Epicurus's Challenge to Our Society: Raising a Tranquil Child "The wise man will marry and beget children, as Epicurus tells us in Problems and his work On Nature; but he will marry according to his station in life, whatever it may be." Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, 10:119. "Natural wealth is limited and easily obtained; the riches of idle fancies go on forever." Principal Doctrine 15. "Some men spend their whole life furnishing for themselves the things proper to life without realizing that at our birth each of us was poured a moral brew to drink." Vatican Sayings 30. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Ch. 17 (pp. 180-190). Some Questions to Discuss: In our society, how realistic is Emily Austin's Epicurean plan for raising a child? What are possible impediments to the realization of her plan? What are possible solutions for overcoming these obstacles?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA; October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation; November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County; January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph. D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/
events.blurb: Join the Graphic Novel Book Club at Mitchell Park Library to discuss the group's latest pick, Thursday evenings.

events.title: Pageturners: The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay by Michael Chabon
events.description: Pageturners read widely, from nonfiction like Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World by Malcolm Harris to fiction like James by Percival Everett to biography like The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI by Fei-Fei Li and graphic novels like The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting Andrey Kurkov (Diary of an Invasion) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. What will we read next? It's anyone's guess. Members suggest books, and then vote on them. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. Our reading list for 2026 follows: My Friends by Fredrik Backman - January; The Wager: A Tale of a Shipwreck, Mutiny and Murder by David Grann - February; South of the Border, West of the Sun by Haruki Murakami - March; Trespassers at the Golden Gate: A True Account of Love, Murder, and Madness in Gilded-Age San Francisco by Gary Krist - April; The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui - May; The Wedding People by Alison Espach - June; Unlikely Animals: A Novel by Annie Hartnett - July; Say Nothing: A True Story of Murder and Memory in Northern Ireland by Patrick Radden Keefe - August; The Frozen River by Ariel Lawhon - September; We'll Prescribe You a Cat by Syou Ishida - October; What We Can Know by Ian McEwan - November; The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay by Michael Chabon - December. You don't have to register, but you will receive a reminder email if you do.
events.blurb: Discuss Michael Chabon's The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay with fellow readers at the Pageturners book group.

events.title: Animal Friends: Meet a Chicken with Isabelle Cnudde
events.description: Did you know chickens can recognize over 100 faces, dream when they sleep, and even see more colors than we do? Join Project Humane Kind at the Palo Alto Children's Library as we meet Clorofil's Isabelle Cnudde and one of her feathered friends. Come discover their natural behaviors, their big personalities, and what makes them such cool animals. Coloring pages will be available for the attendees. Registration required. Note: Registrations will be released for standby attendees at the start of the program. Please arrive on time. As founder of Clorofil, an animal advocacy nonprofit and micro-sanctuary, Isabelle rescues chickens and gives them a safe home where they can just be chickens. Learn more about them at www.clorofil.org. Project Humane Kind teaches compassion and respect for living beings. Through humane education, they combat cruelty and indifference and bring awareness to the intelligent, social, and emotional depths of our fellow animals. Visit them online at www.projecthumanekind.org.
events.blurb: Meet Clorofil's Isabelle Cnudde and her chicken to learn surprising facts about how chickens see, dream, and recognize faces.

events.description: Join us for a special Yalda Night celebration with children's author Anahita Tamaddon and a reading of her book, Yalda Night! Experience the beauty of this cherished Persian tradition through a Yalda-inspired story, music, and a fun paper craft featuring one of Yalda's beloved symbols. Yalda, the longest night of the year, is a joyful celebration of family, storytelling, and togetherness as we welcome the arrival of winter. All craft materials will be provided. Children ages three and up, along with their adult caregivers, are invited to participate. Materials will be available while supplies last. While registration isn't required and doesn't guarantee a spot, it is recommended if you'd like a reminder about the event. برای جشن ویژه‌ی شب یلدا همراه با نویسنده‌ی کتاب‌های کودک، آناهیتا تمدن ، به ما بپیوندیددر این برنامه با زیبایی‌های این سنت دیرینه‌ی ایرانی از طریق قصه‌ای با حال‌وهوای یلدا، موسیقی و ساخت کاردستی کاغذی با الهام از یکی از نمادهای دوست‌داشتنی یلدا آشنا خواهیم شد. شب یلدا، بلندترین شب سال، فرصتی برای جشن گرفتن در کنار خانواده و عزیزان، قصه‌گویی و با هم بودن و همچنین خوشامدگویی به فصل زمستان است. تمام وسایل مورد نیاز برای ساخت کاردستی فراهم خواهد بود.

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA; October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation; November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County; January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph. D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/
events.blurb: Join the Graphic Novel Book Club at Mitchell Park Library to discuss the group's latest pick, Thursday evenings.

events.title: Pageturners: Double Play on the Red Line with Raj Oza
events.description: Join us for a special discussion with local author Raj Oza about his book Double Play on the Red Line. Here's a chance to talk to a writer about his writing process and to hear how he came to write this novel. Pageturners read widely, from nonfiction like Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World by Malcolm Harris to fiction like James by Percival Everett to biography like The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI by Fei-Fei Li and graphic novels like The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting International Booker Prize winner Andrey Kurkov (Diary of an Invasion) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. What will we read next? It's anyone's guess. Members suggest books, and then vote on them. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. You don't have to register, but you will receive a reminder email if you do.
events.blurb: Talk with local author Raj Oza about Double Play on the Red Line and hear how he came to write the novel.

events.title: Open Sewing Studio
events.description: Do you have a sewing project but need the equipment and space? Are you interested in learning about the basics of a sewing machine? Open Sewing Studio is a space for both beginners looking to learn as well as experienced sewists looking for the time and space to work on their project. We will have sewing machines, table space, fabric scraps, and tools available for attendees. Bring your own projects and have fun! Note: Teens and adults only. Use of machines will be on a first-come, first-served basis due to limited supply. Our staff is only available to support very basic projects. events.title: Mindfulness Meditation
events.description: Come and improve your mental and physical health in mindfulness meditation sessions led by Phuong Pham. Each session is 30 minutes of sitting meditation and 15 minutes of releasing meditation followed by 15 minutes of group sharing and Q&A. It is open to all levels of experience and no registration is required. Participants are encouraged to bring their own yoga mats and/or meditation cushions. Chairs are available for those who do not bring them. Phuong is a Buddhist nun experienced in leading mindfulness meditation. You can learn more about Phuong here and can watch her meditation videos on the library's YouTube channel here.
events.blurb: Sit for guided sitting and releasing meditation with Phuong Pham, then join a group sharing and Q&A session.

Playing Mahjong improves cognitive function, helps reduce stress, and creates a sense of community. This program is suitable for adults and seniors. Free. Registration required. events.title: English Language Learners (ELL) Conversation Club
events.description: This program is in-person at Educational Park Branch Library. Are you looking for a place to practice your English conversation skills in a fun, welcoming and safe environment? Look no further! Our English Language Learners (ELL) Conversation Club offers a respectful environment for adult learners of English to practice their English speaking & conversation skills used in everyday settings. All levels of English speaking skills are welcome!

events.title: Friends of the Campbell Library Used Book Sale
events.description: Join us for the Friends of the Campbell Library used book sale! Items for sale include puzzles, games, hardback fiction books, children's books, romances, thrillers, audio books, DVDs, CDs, and a variety of 'how to' books. Pay cash, check, Zelle, card, or Venmo. Remember to bring a bag for your purchases! Sign up to hear about more upcoming Book Sales at the Friends of the Campbell Library's website: Sales - Friends of the Campbell Library

events.title: Saturday STEM: Haunted House Engineering
events.description: Join us for Saturday STEM! Kids will explore a fun STEM activity focused on the theme of the day. Kids will practice their engineering skills by building their own Graham Cracker Haunted House for Halloween! Space is limited to 15 participants, and tickets will be available at the Front Desk one hour before the event begins to secure a spot. Tickets and supplies are available on a first-come, first-served basis. We hope to see you there!

events.title: Reading to Children
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading, and learning. events.description: Drop in for a full day of modern board gaming at the Downtown Library! The group meets every 1st Saturday from 10 AM–6 PM. events.title: Ukraine: Culture, Geography, History and Heritage
events.description: Nora Mason, a native-born Ukrainian and long-time Saratoga resident, will present a program on the culture of Ukraine and how its geography has contributed to tragic invasions over time. She will share her family's WWII story and how they ultimately immigrated to the United States. She will also touch on inspiring efforts to help the people of Ukraine today. Program co-sponsored by the Los Gatos-Saratoga AAUW.
events.blurb: Hear Ukrainian-born Saratoga resident Nora Mason talk about Ukraine's culture and how its geography has shaped its history of invasions.

Want to push yourself and try something a little more difficult? Ask the librarian for a Lego Challenge! Important: Children under 5 must be accompanied by their parents as small LEGO pieces can be choking hazards.

events.title: Resume Review & Interview Preparation
events.description: A well-crafted resume is vital for standing out to potential employers. Our volunteer will help you learn the essential elements of a successful resume and prepare for interviews. Gain expert tips on highlighting your accomplishments, showcasing transferable skills, and mastering the STAR framework to ace your next interview. No registration required. #sjplworkscareer
events.blurb: Work with a volunteer to polish your resume and practice answers for upcoming job interviews.

events.title: Family Craft: Bean and Lentil Mosaics
events.description: Choose from a variety of beans and lentils to create your own colorful mosaic! Children ages 4–11 are invited to make a unique design using paper, glue, beans, and lentils. All materials will be provided. Family Craft events are designed for children and their adult companions to enjoy together. Crafts will be available while supplies last, so please arrive on time.
events.blurb: Design a colorful mosaic from beans and lentils in this hands-on family craft session.

events.title: TeenHQ: Pipe Cleaner Flowers
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Come hang out in TeenHQ and create fun and long-lasting flower bouquets out of pipe cleaners. This event takes place in TeenHQ and is for Middle and High Schoolers (grades 6-12) only. Adults and younger relations can wait for teens in the TeenHQ Reading Room. Parking at King Library: It is recommended to park at the 4th Street Garage. The first 90 minutes are free.
events.blurb: Make pipe cleaner flower bouquets in TeenHQ at King Library, an afternoon session for grades 6-12.

events.title: Chair Yoga with Patricia Becker
events.description: Join established local yoga teacher Patricia Becker as she takes us through exercises to loosen joints, improve flexibility, improve cognition, and increase strength in Rinconada Library's Embarcadero Room. Registration isn't needed but means you will receive an email reminder. Here are the dates for 2027: January 2; March 6; May 1; July 3; September 4; November 6.
events.attendanceNote: Registration is not required. Optional signup provides an email reminder.
events.blurb: Move through seated stretches with Patricia Becker to loosen joints and build strength in the Embarcadero Room.

events.title: Knitting / Crocheting / Tatting / Bobbin Lace Club
events.address: 1102 E Santa Clara St San Jose
events.description: Do you enjoy working with knitting, crocheting, or tatting? Do you want to learn how, see what others are working on, refine your skills, or talk about all kinds of hand needle crafts? Join us in the East San Jose Carnegie Branch Community Room every week. Everyone 7 and up is invited to participate, and younger children are welcome to accompany their families.
events.blurb: Bring your knitting, crocheting, or tatting project to work alongside other crafters and swap tips.

There will be a Halloween-themed storytime, a parade with a chance for trick-or-treating throughout the library and an assortment of grab-and-go arts and crafts to choose from that are suitable for all ages. Please wear your costumes, if possible! Free. Registration not required.
events.blurb: Join the Halloween Festival at Joyce Ellington Library on a Saturday afternoon with your family.
